questions.prompt: In Claude Code, in which order are permission rules evaluated?

options.explanation: That would let an allow rule override a deny. The order is the other way round.
The docs say rule specificity doesn't change the order.

options.text: Deny, then ask, then allow; the first match wins
options.explanation: Right. So a broad deny blocks a call even when a narrower allow also matches.

questions.prompt: In the Claude Agent SDK, `disallowed_tools` contains the bare name `Bash`. What happens?

options.text: The Bash tool is removed, so Claude doesn't see it and can't try it
options.explanation: Right. A scoped rule like `Bash(rm *)` would keep the tool and block only matching calls.

options.text: Claude can call Bash, but every call asks for approval
options.explanation: That is what an ask rule does. A bare-name deny removes the tool.

options.text: Bash is blocked except in `bypassPermissions` mode
options.explanation: Deny rules hold in every mode, including `bypassPermissions`.

questions.prompt: An OpenAI Agents SDK tool has `needs_approval=True`. What happens when the model calls it?

options.text: The tool runs, and a human reviews the result afterwards.
options.explanation: The run pauses before the tool executes. Review happens first.

options.text: The run fails with an exception and must start over.
options.explanation: It is a pause, not a failure. You resume the same run from its state.

options.text: The run pauses with an interruption; after approve or reject, you resume from `state`.
options.explanation: Right. If review takes time, you can store the serialized state and continue the same run later.
